$documentation: Enumerated exceptions for the blocking dependency-audit gate (scripts/audit-gate.mjs,
run by the `audit` job in .github/workflows/test.yml). Policy narrative lives in
Every advisory `bun audit` reports must either be FIXED or appear here. There is no
third option and no global escape hatch: this file replaced a `continue-on-error` +
`|| echo` pair whose justification ('all in harper transitive deps') was true when it
was written, carried no expiry, and was still silently passing the build long after it
Adding an entry is a REVIEWED act, not a way to get green. Each one must carry the
advisory id, what pulls it in, why it cannot be fixed from this repo, a hard expiry
date, and the concrete condition that retires it. The gate enforces all of that
mechanically, including a severity-scaled cap on how long an entry may live — you
cannot park a critical for a year.
When an entry expires the build FAILS and a human re-decides. That is the mechanism
working. Re-dating an entry without re-reading its reason is how this file rots back

classes.no-patch-published: No fixed version exists on the registry yet. Verified by the gate on every run: if a patched version ships, this entry fails and must be actioned.
classes.vendor-pinned: A patched version exists upstream, but the vulnerable copy is resolved inside a vendored dependency whose tree we do not control. Retired by moving the vendor, not by bumping the leaf.
classes.remediation-available: A patched version exists AND we could take it. Deliberately deferred to a separate, test-gated dependency PR so a security gate lands independently of a lockfile change. Shortest leash of the three.

entries.introducedBy: harper -> micromatch -> braces; harper -> fast-glob -> micromatch -> braces; @tpsdev-ai/adk-flair (packages/adk-flair-js) -> @google/adk -> (@mikro-orm/core | @mikro-orm/reflection) -> globby -> fast-glob -> micromatch -> braces (bun workspace only)
entries.reason: Renewed 2026-10-07 after re-reading against harper 5.2.8, the version flair pins (first added 2026-10-03). No fixed release exists: npm's latest braces is 3.0.3, inside the affected range (<=3.0.3). Resolved copies: one in bun.lock (braces 3.0.3, under micromatch 4.0.8) and harper 5.2.8's npm-shrinkwrap pin 3.0.3 (node_modules/harper/node_modules/braces in an npm install of flair). In bun.lock it is reached through harper's micromatch ^4.0.8 and fast-glob 3.3.3 and, in the bun workspace only, through @google/adk 1.6.0 -> @mikro-orm/core and @mikro-orm/reflection 6.6.16 -> globby 11.1.0 -> fast-glob; an npm install of flair carries only the harper path. flair's own code does not import braces, micromatch or fast-glob. Runtime discovery reaches braces through fast-glob's pattern expansion (node_modules/.bun/fast-glob@3.3.3/node_modules/fast-glob/out/utils/pattern.js:137), and micromatch returns a pattern without brace syntax unchanged before calling braces (node_modules/.bun/micromatch@4.0.8/node_modules/micromatch/index.js:451-456). harper 5.2.8 passes fast-glob component config source/ignore patterns (node_modules/harper/dist/components/ComponentV1.js:225), loadEnv files patterns (node_modules/harper/dist/config/componentEnvPrepass.js:162) and paths built from the configured components root and the project directories under it (node_modules/harper/dist/components/operations.js:55,60,63). flair's shipped patterns are fixed and contain no brace syntax (.env, schemas/*.graphql, dist/resources/*.js; config.yaml:4,6,8). Request-time matching uses configured patterns, not the URL as a pattern (node_modules/harper/dist/server/static.js:79), and isMatch and scan delegate to picomatch, not braces (micromatch/index.js:128,408). No request-to-braces-pattern path was found in flair or harper; whoever can write harper's component configuration or its components-root directory remains a denial-of-service risk. The ADK adapter imports SDK types only (packages/adk-flair-js/src/memory_service.ts:15-18). As a no-patch-published entry, the gate blocks it once npm's latest braces is outside the affected range (when the audit can reach the registry). Expiry aligned with the other harper-pinned high entries.
entries.removeWhen: A braces release outside this advisory's vulnerable range is published, a harper release whose npm-shrinkwrap resolves it is adopted, and every bun path resolves it (or those paths are removed); re-check config and filesystem pattern inputs before renewal.

entries.reason: Renewed 2026-10-07 after re-reading against harper 5.2.8, the version flair pins (first added 2026-07-27; renewed 2026-09-25). Resolved copies: one in bun.lock (@fastify/static 9.3.0, pulled only by harper ^9.1.3) and harper 5.2.8's npm-shrinkwrap pin 9.3.0 (node_modules/harper/node_modules/@fastify/static in an npm install of flair). The fix is 10.1.1 (10.1.2 for GHSA-8pvw-jcv7-9cmj; npm's latest is 10.1.5), and the 9.x line ends at 9.3.0 with no backport. Every published harper line still declares ^9.1.3 (5.2.8; 5.2.15, latest-5.2; 5.3.1, latest; 5.3.0-beta.4, next), so the fix is a major bump inside harper's HTTP layer that a root override would force on the server harper itself mounts. Where it is used: harper 5.2.8 imports it only in dist/server/operationsServer.js:53 and registers it once (:210), on the operations server, with a fixed root of harper's own Studio assets (studio/web); flair's localStudio enabled: false (src/commands/init.ts:963) changes only which page the / handler serves (:211-217), not that registration. That file adds no request hook; authentication on the operations server is per-route preValidation (GET /api/openapi/rest :219, POST / :222), so no guard is tied to the paths the plugin serves. harper's application-port static handler uses send, not this plugin (dist/server/static.js:12), and flair's component config mounts no static files (config.yaml). flair does not import @fastify/static. The default flair install binds the operations server to 127.0.0.1 (src/cli.ts:564) plus an owner-only domain socket (src/commands/init.ts:950,961; posture at src/cli.ts:1824-1831); an operator who widens that bind with --ops-bind or FLAIR_OPS_BIND makes the plugin reachable beyond loopback. Short leash (14 days) pending the upstream move.
entries.removeWhen: flair moves to a harper release whose npm-shrinkwrap resolves @fastify/static >=10.1.1 (>=10.1.2 also retires GHSA-8pvw-jcv7-9cmj), or flair stops depending on harper; as of 2026-10-07 no published harper release does (5.2.15, 5.3.1 and 5.3.0-beta.4 all declare ^9.1.3).

entries.reason: O(depth-squared) event-loop DoS in stream-json's pick/ignore/filter/replace filters on crafted nested JSON. stream-json@1.9.1 is a transitive pin of harper (@harperfast/harper; harper 5.2.x); it cannot be overridden from this repo (harper ships an npm-shrinkwrap and the override is bun-only, flair#1498/#1510). flair does not import stream-json directly - reachability is only via harper's internal streaming parser, not flair code.
entries.removeWhen: harper ships a build resolving stream-json > 3.4.0 (the patched line), or flair stops depending on harper.

entries.reason: Prototype pollution in stream-json's Assembler (fixed in 3.6.0). Harper 5.2.8 pins stream-json 1.9.1 in its npm-shrinkwrap, which blocks a root override for npm installs (flair#1498/#1510). A Bun root override to stream-json 3.x is deferred pending compatibility testing. flair does not import stream-json. Harper 5.2.8 imports StreamArray and Batch in dist/dataLayer/bulkLoad.js; its import_from_s3 operation selects JSON from the S3 object's extension. StreamArray builds each element through the Assembler, so that path is in scope; Harper checks target-table insert permission for an insert import, update permission for update, and both for upsert (dist/utility/operation_authorization.js).
entries.removeWhen: harper ships a build resolving stream-json >= 3.6.0, or flair stops depending on harper.

A Bun root override to stream-json 3.x is deferred pending compatibility testing. flair does not import stream-json. Harper 5.2.8 imports StreamArray and Batch in dist/dataLayer/bulkLoad.js; its import_from_s3 operation selects JSON from the S3 object's extension.
entries.removeWhen: harper ships a build resolving stream-json > 3.5.0, or flair stops depending on harper; re-check this entry if harper moves to a stream-json major that includes the JSONC parser.

entries.reason: Transitive via harper@5.2.8 shrinkwrap (joi pinned 17.13.4). The root override (joi ^17.13.7) resolves 17.13.8 in bun.lock, so only npm installs still carry the pin, which that override does not reach (flair#1498/#1510). Flair authors no joi schemas (no direct joi import or schema in the source, so no joi schema rename call); the vuln requires object().rename(regex, Joi.x(), {multiple:true}) which Flair does not use - not reachable in Flair code. Residual is harper's internal joi usage, which is un-audited (bundled dep). Security sign-off: tps-sherlock 2026-09-09.
entries.removeWhen: harper ships a build resolving joi >=17.13.5 (out of the vulnerable range), or flair stops depending on harper. Re-evaluate on ANY harper version bump; if harper ships a release note touching joi rename/validation, re-check before the next merge.

entries.reason: Transitive via harper@5.2.8 shrinkwrap (joi pinned 17.13.4). The root override (joi ^17.13.7) resolves 17.13.8 in bun.lock, so only npm installs still carry the pin, which that override does not reach. Prototype pollution via a __proto__ language key in joi's custom message config (messages/message/prefs({messages})/Joi.extend/rule({message})); trigger is attacker-controlled data passed into joi message config. Flair authors zero joi schemas AND zero joi message config (no joi import, no Joi.extend, no prefs/messages usage in the repo) - not reachable in Flair code. Residual is harper's internal joi usage, un-audited (bundled dep); message config is almost always static developer strings, not runtime data. Security sign-off: tps-sherlock 2026-09-09.

entries.reason: Prototype replacement through message codes in joi's message compilation (fixed in 17.13.8). Resolved inside harper's pinned npm-shrinkwrap (joi 17.13.4 in harper 5.2.8), which npm honours over root overrides (flair#1498/#1510). The root override (joi ^17.13.7) already resolves 17.13.8 in bun.lock, so only npm installs carry the pin. flair imports no joi. The fix is confined to joi's handling of message-code keys when it compiles or merges message configuration (node_modules/harper/node_modules/joi/lib/messages.js compile and merge). Harper's .messages calls pass object literals with fixed code keys (for example node_modules/harper/dist/components/operationsValidation.js:105, dist/dataLayer/schema.js:72-90, dist/security/certificateVerification/configValidation.js:41-49, dist/validation/statusValidator.js:70-72, dist/validation/deleteValidator.js:48).
entries.removeWhen: flair's harper dependency moves to 5.3.0 or later (harper 5.3.0's shrinkwrap resolves joi 17.13.8), or flair stops depending on harper.

entries.reason: Published 2026-09-29. moment is an exact dependency of harper itself: harper 5.2.8 (the version flair pins) through 5.2.14 depend on moment 2.30.1 and pin it in their npm-shrinkwrap, which npm honours over root overrides. harper 5.3.0, the latest, depends on and pins 2.31.0, the fixed version. The bun override (moment ^2.31.0, added for this advisory) keeps bun.lock on 2.31.0, but npm installs carry harper 5.2.8's pin. flair does not import moment. The leash is 60 days rather than the 180-day moderate cap because a fixed harper release already exists, so retiring this entry is flair's own harper bump.
entries.removeWhen: flair's harper dependency moves to 5.3.0 or later (harper 5.3.0's shrinkwrap resolves moment 2.31.0), or flair stops depending on harper

entries.reason: Renewed 2026-10-07 after re-reading against harper 5.2.8, the version flair pins (first added 2026-10-02). No fixed release exists: npm's latest node-forge is 1.4.0, inside the affected range (<=1.4.0). Resolved copies: one in bun.lock (node-forge 1.4.0, pulled only by harper ^1.3.1) and harper 5.2.8's npm-shrinkwrap pin 1.4.0 (node_modules/harper/node_modules/node-forge in an npm install of flair); harper 5.2.8, 5.2.15, 5.3.1 and 5.3.0-beta.4 all declare ^1.3.1. flair's own code does not import it. harper 5.2.8's only import is node_modules/harper/dist/security/keys.js:64, which uses forge.pki to create and sign its CA and server certificates (generateCertificates :543-567, generateCertAuthority :589-613) and to parse and PEM-encode keys and certificates (:491, :538-539, :547, :617, :649, :689, :695, :706, :708). keys.js never calls node-forge's RSA signature verification, the path this advisory affects. As a no-patch-published entry, the gate blocks it once npm's latest node-forge is outside the affected range (when the audit can reach the registry). Expiry aligned with the other harper-pinned high entries.
entries.removeWhen: npm's latest node-forge release is outside the affected range (the gate then blocks this entry): reassess; a maintainer removes the entry once harper resolves a fixed release or drops node-forge

entries.reason: Gap in simple-git's unsafe-operation guard (affected >=3.15.0 <4.0.1). simple-git@3.36.0 arrives through @tpsdev-ai/flair-bench -> node-llama-cpp@3.18.1, which declares simple-git ^3.33.0 (packages/flair-bench/package.json; node-llama-cpp/package.json). node-llama-cpp calls simple-git through its source-build clone (dist/bindings/getLlama.js -> utils/compileLLamaCpp.js -> utils/cloneLlamaCppRepo.js) and its source download CLI clone with CLI-supplied repo and release values (dist/cli/commands/source/commands/DownloadCommand.js). That CLI also calls dist/utils/gitReleaseBundles.js under its CI bundle flag. Flair and flair-bench do not invoke that CLI path. flair-bench calls getLlama() with default options (packages/flair-bench/src/engine.ts); the source-build clone uses built-in defaults or NODE_LLAMA_CPP_REPO and NODE_LLAMA_CPP_REPO_RELEASE (dist/config.js). Remediation-available, deferred: the simple-git 4.0.2 root override crosses node-llama-cpp's declared range and belongs in a separate, test-gated dependency PR that exercises the source-build clone.
entries.removeWhen: a separate, test-gated PR overrides simple-git to >=4.0.2 after exercising node-llama-cpp's source-build clone, or node-llama-cpp ships a release declaring simple-git >=4.0.1 and flair-bench moves to it, or flair-bench drops node-llama-cpp.

entries.reason: Denial of service in sprintf-js's handling of precision specifiers. sprintf-js@1.1.3 reaches the workspace lockfile through @tpsdev-ai/adk-flair -> @google/adk@1.6.0, which declares the mikro-orm SQL drivers, including @mikro-orm/mssql, as non-optional peers; @mikro-orm/mssql@6.6.16 depends on tedious@19.2.1, which depends on sprintf-js. tedious's calls pass a literal format string (node_modules/tedious/lib/packet.js:131,144,155; lib/metadata-parser.js:104,355; lib/value-parser.js:409,485; lib/prelogin-payload.js:223; lib/login7-payload.js:419). As a no-patch-published entry, the gate blocks it once npm's latest sprintf-js is outside the affected range (when the audit can reach the registry).
entries.removeWhen: npm's latest sprintf-js release is outside the affected range (the gate then blocks this entry): move to it with a root override, or remove the entry once tedious, @mikro-orm/mssql or @google/adk stop pulling sprintf-js into bun.lock.
